prompt: Complete IntStats.minMaxSum, returning {min, max, sum} for an int array ({0, 0, 0} when the array is empty); IntStream makes this a three-liner.
explanation: IntStream.of(values) streams a primitive int array without boxing. Because min() and max() are undefined for an empty stream they return OptionalInt, which is why the empty case is handled up front with an early return. summaryStatistics() computes min, max, sum (and count/average) in a single pass -- neater than running three separate terminal operations over three separate streams.
hints: Handle the empty array first: if values.length == 0, return new int[] { 0, 0, 0 }.
java.util.stream.IntStream.of(values).summaryStatistics() gives an object with getMin(), getMax() and getSum().
getSum() returns a long, so cast it to int when building the result array.
